questions.question_text: Mr. X is a 56-year-old gentleman assessed in the outpatient clinic. He is presenting with features of alcohol withdrawal. The patient is asked to complete Short Alcohol Withdrawal Scale. The nurse wants to know the total scores, above which he might require pharmacotherapy for withdrawal. Choose the correct answer from the following options.
questions.explanation: (SAWS) short alcohol withdrawal scale is a self-completion questionnaire. Total scores above 12 require pharmacotherapy.

questions.question_text: The maximum possible score from General Health Questionnaire (28 items version) is
questions.explanation: The maximum possible score on the GHQ 28 is 84.

questions.question_text: Which of the following rating scale for depression has more cognitive items than the others?
questions.explanation: The Beck Depression Inventory (BDI - II) is a 21-item measure designed to assess the cognitive, behavioral, affective and somatic symptoms of depression.

questions.question_text: Which of the following rating scales for depression used in adults is well validated in children aged 14 and older?
questions.explanation: BDI is validated for use in those who are above 14 years of age.

questions.question_text: You want to screen for depression in adolescents of age between 14 and 18-years. Which is the best screening tool?

options.text: Child and adolescent functional assessment scale

questions.explanation: BDI can be used to screen depression above 14 years age.

questions.question_text: Which one among the following rating scales is a self-administered instrument?
questions.explanation: Beck depression inventory is a self-rating scale with 21 items measuring the severity of depression.

questions.question_text: Which of the following refers to the extent to which performance on a test fits with theoretical schema about the test attributes?
questions.explanation: Construct validity refers to the degree to which inferences can legitimately be made from the operationalizations in a study to the theoretical constructs on which those operationalizations were based.

questions.question_text: Concurrent validity is also known as
questions.explanation: In criterion-related validity, we examine whether the operationalised criteria used in a scale is aligned to the theory behind a construct that is being tested.

questions.question_text: In psychometry internal consistency refers to

options.text: Degree of agreement between results obtained in two different occasions
Degree of correlation between one test item with other items
Degree of agreement between two similar scales
Degree of agreement between two raters
Degree of correlation between two different versions of the scale

correct_answer.text: Degree of correlation between one test item with other items

correct_answers.text: Degree of correlation between one test item with other items

questions.explanation: In internal consistency, we measure how well the items that reflect the same construct yield similar results.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a self-rated questionnaire used as a screening instrument for the presence of psychiatric illness?
questions.explanation: General Health Questionnaire (GHQ) is a self-rated questionnaire used as a screening instrument for the presence of psychiatric illness.

questions.question_text: A tool designed to test cognitive functions has subtests that measure cognitive abilities well. This test can be said to have
questions.explanation: Construct validity seeks agreement between a theoretical concept and a specific measuring device or procedure.

questions.question_text: All of the following are projective tests except
questions.explanation: HAMD is a test for depression - it is not a projective test.

questions.question_text: The SF-36 scale measures which of the following?
questions.explanation: Health-related quality of life (HRQOL) refers to functioning and well-being in physical, mental and social dimensions of life, and the SF-36 is commonly used to assess it.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following scales is used for monitoring clinical recovery?
questions.explanation: Health of the Nation Outcome Scales (HoNOS) was specifically designed as an outcome indicator for monitoring clinical change.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a type of validity?
questions.explanation: Inter-rater reliability is different from validity.

questions.question_text: Considering Beck's Depression Inventory, which of the following is true?

options.text: Refers to symptoms over the last five days.
Has no item on suicidal ideas

questions.explanation: Beck Depression Inventory was created by Dr. Aaron T. Beck. It is a 21-question multiple-choice self-report inventory.

questions.question_text: With respect to Young Mania Rating Scale, which of the following is least likely to be correct?

options.text: Psychotic symptoms are not included in the scale
It does not have items on suicidality

questions.explanation: Young Mania Rating Scale is clinician-rated.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct concerning the SCID?

options.text: Provides the Axis V diagnosis in DSM-IV.
Based on a dimensional diagnostic scheme
Used in conjunction with ICD-10 classification

questions.explanation: Structured Clinical Interview for DSM (SCID) is primarily used in research with trained interviewers.

questions.question_text: Which of the following rating scales retain the aspects of a clinical examination during consultation?
questions.explanation: PSE retains the aspects of a mental state examination.

questions.question_text: The Clifton Assessment Procedure is used in which of the following situations?

options.text: Care homes for the learning disabled
Prisons with high mental health burden

questions.explanation: The Clifton Assessment Procedure is widely used in elderly residential care settings.

questions.question_text: Which of the following interview schedules have replaced the Present Status Examination in contemporary epidemiological studies?
questions.explanation: SCAN stands for Schedules for Clinical Assessment in Neuropsychiatry and replaces PSE.

questions.question_text: Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale is a clinician-rated scale used to measure the severity of clinical symptoms based on observation. It is most commonly used in patients with a diagnosis of
questions.explanation: BPRS measures major psychotic and non-psychotic symptoms, primarily used for schizophrenia patients.

questions.question_text: What is the most reliable instrument to make clinical diagnosis according to DSM criteria?
questions.explanation: The structured clinical interview for the DSM (SCID) is arguably the most reliable instrument for psychiatric diagnoses.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not an alcohol assessment tool?
questions.explanation: SCOFF is an eating disorders questionnaire, not an alcohol assessment tool.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a rating scale for mood disorders?
questions.explanation: Simpson Angus Rating scale is used to measure extrapyramidal symptoms.

questions.question_text: Which of the following technique is best utilised minimally if possible in those with high suggestibility?
questions.explanation: Structured interviews have demonstrated a high degree of reliability, validity, and legal defensibility.

questions.question_text: The term test-retest reliability refers to

options.text: The correlation between the 1st and 2nd test in the same subject
Degree of correlation between two different versions of the scale.
Degree of agreement between two raters.
The correlation between the 1st and 2nd test of a number of subjects.
The correlation between two different raters.

correct_answer.text: The correlation between the 1st and 2nd test in the same subject

correct_answers.text: The correlation between the 1st and 2nd test in the same subject

questions.explanation: Test-Retest Reliability measures the ability of a psychological testing instrument to yield the same result for a single subject at 2 different test periods.

questions.question_text: You have designed a study questionnaire and would like to measure the inter-rater reliability. Which of the following will you be testing?

options.text: The questionnaire is valid when it gives same results if assessed by two different assessors on two different patients
The scores given by one rater are well concealed and cannot be copied by another rater
The questionnaire is valid when it gives same results if assessed on two different occasions by same rater
The questionnaire gives same results when used by two different raters on the same patient
Self-rating and clinician rating gives the same score from the questionnaire

correct_answer.text: The questionnaire gives same results when used by two different raters on the same patient

correct_answers.text: The questionnaire gives same results when used by two different raters on the same patient

questions.explanation: Inter-rater reliability refers to the consistency among different raters using a scale.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a gold standard test for intelligence?
questions.explanation: WAIS is the gold standard intelligence measurement scale that can be used from ages 16 to 89.

questions.question_text: A 22-year-old man is admitted with troublesome voices discussing his sexuality. He also believes they influence his actions and control his thoughts. Which of the following instrument can be used to monitor his symptoms?

options.text: Schedule for Assessment of Negative symptoms

questions.explanation: BPRS is useful to monitor changes in positive psychotic symptoms.

questions.question_text: Which of the following scales can be used by primary care physicians, general medical professionals and also in community studies?

options.text: Scale of Assessment of Positive Symptoms
Signs and Symptoms in Psychotic Illness

questions.explanation: The GHQ is well-validated and widely used in studies to detect 'caseness'.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most important aspect of construct validity for a test of cognitive impairment in dementia?

options.text: It includes most of the components of cognition that is commonly affected by dementia
It predicts the likelihood of progression to end stage dementia
The scores depend on educational attainment of the subjects
Experts agree with the choice of sub items for the global scale
Scores are not affected by taking medications

correct_answer.text: It includes most of the components of cognition that is commonly affected by dementia

correct_answers.text: It includes most of the components of cognition that is commonly affected by dementia

questions.explanation: Construct validity specifies the extent to which the items and assessments effectively reflect the construct being measured.

questions.question_text: Which of the following scales is used for measuring drug-induced movement abnormalities in general and tardive dyskinesia in particular?
questions.explanation: The Abnormal involuntary movements scale is used to examine tardive dyskinesia.

questions.question_text: The assessment tool useful in measuring the severity and change in psychotic symptoms is
questions.explanation: BPRS was designed to assess psychopathology including various psychotic symptoms.

questions.question_text: You have designed a study questionnaire and would like to measure the construct validity. Which of the following will you be testing?

options.text: Constituent parts of the questionnaire are suitable and related to the phenomenon being tested
The questionnaire predicts what will happen in the future
The questionnaire covers most symptoms related to the phenomenon being measured
The questionnaire gives same results when tested on the same patient twice by a single rater
The questionnaire gives same results when used by two different raters on the same patient twice

correct_answer.text: Constituent parts of the questionnaire are suitable and related to the phenomenon being tested

correct_answers.text: Constituent parts of the questionnaire are suitable and related to the phenomenon being tested

questions.explanation: Construct validity evaluates if the test appropriately represents the concept it is intended to measure.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following questionnaires can be used to identify psychiatric 'caseness' in the general population?
questions.explanation: GHQ was developed as a screening tool to detect those likely to have or be at risk of developing psychiatric disorders.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct statement about Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale?

options.text: It is an assessment of global psychiatric symptomatology
Each item is rated on a 6-point scale

correct_answer.text: It is an assessment of global psychiatric symptomatology

correct_answers.text: It is an assessment of global psychiatric symptomatology

questions.explanation: BPRS assesses various psychiatric symptoms to evaluate the severity of conditions.

questions.question_text: Which of the following scales is NOT used for measuring drug-induced movement abnormalities?
questions.explanation: Lane scale is not designed for measuring drug-induced movement abnormalities.

questions.question_text: Mr. Y is a 30-year-old man who presented to the A and E after an overdose. He believes that there are cameras spying on his movements. He has stopped going out and no longer socializes with friends. He has been hearing voices discussing his sexuality in an unpleasant way. Which of the following tools would be helpful to assess and monitor his psychopathology?
questions.explanation: PANSS provides a balanced representation of positive and negative symptoms useful for monitoring centrally.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true concerning Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale (BPRS)?

options.text: Useful for global psychiatric symptom ratings
Cannot be used to detect treatment response
It requires no clinical training to administer

correct_answer.text: Useful for global psychiatric symptom ratings

correct_answers.text: Useful for global psychiatric symptom ratings

questions.explanation: BPRS is specifically designed to quantify various psychiatric symptoms and monitor changes in response to treatment.

questions.question_text: Which of the following scales of depression is most sensitive to change?
questions.explanation: Montgomery-Asberg depression rating scale is specifically designed to capture changes in symptoms over time.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a useful screening tool for early detection of an eating disorder?
questions.explanation: SCOFF questionnaire is a screening tool consisting of questions that help in identifying key symptoms of eating disorders.

questions.question_text: Which is the most commonly used screening tool to diagnose dementia in older people?
questions.explanation: The Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) is the most widely used cognitive test in geriatrics, effective for screening dementia.
